newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-ELLWOOD UPSETS SERNA TO LEVEL TIE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ELLWOOD UPSETS SERNA TO LEVEL TIE.

text.p: Australia, without a player in the world's top 60, held 1995 winners Spain 1-1 after the first day of their Fed Cup World Group play-off on Saturday.
Australia number one Annabel Ellwood, ranked 66, beat Spain's Maria Luisa Serna 6-4 6-2 to level the tie on the hardcourts at the Hope Island resort in Queensland.
World number eight Arantxa Sanchez Vicario earlier thrashed Rachel McQuillan, ranked 106, 6-2 6-1 to put the visitors ahead after the opening rubber.
The winner of the tie, to be completed on Sunday with the doubles and the reverse singles, will play in the eight-nation elite World Group next season.
Serna, who is ranked 22 places above Ellwood, appeared to lose her composure after questioning a line call late in the first set.
After the match, Serna said the decision may have affected her concentration in the second set.
"It hurts a little bit," Serna said later about her defeat.
Ellwood, whose performance was described as a "terrific job" by team captain Liz Smylie, said her opponent's apparent distress was an increasingly important factor in the match.
"I thought in the second set she gave me a few extra free points maybe because she was a little bit on edge," Ellwood said.
Smylie said of Ellwood: "With Australia one-nil down in the tie, all the pressure was there and she just handled it perfectly."
Spain, winners of the Cup four times in the past six years, were weakened by the absence of former Wimbledon champion Conchita Martinez, who opted to miss the tie.
Sanchez Vicario will team up with Serna in the doubles on Sunday against Australia's McQuillan and Kristine Kunce.
